decision.explanation: The question 'When was the Croatian money introduced?' refers to two distinct historical introductions of the kuna found in the sources. D2S5, D3S2, and D4S1 confirm the first introduction of the 'Independent State of Croatia kuna' (often referred to as Croatian money in that context) on '26 July 1941'. D1S3 confirms the introduction of the 'modern kuna' (the current currency) on 'May 30, 1994'. Both dates represent valid instances of 'Croatian money' being introduced, corresponding to different eras and entities (NDH vs. modern Republic), thus both are preserved as complementary answers.
